_comment_rewrites: Firebase Hosting is the CloudFront equivalent: a global CDN with free-tier
TLS and custom domains, and -- critically -- NO forwarding rule. The literal
GCP analogue of CloudFront-in-front-of-S3 is Cloud CDN behind a global
external Application Load Balancer, which bills ~$18/month before the first
request. Firebase Hosting is $0 idle. See docs/adr/005-firebase-hosting.md.
Rewrites are FIRST-MATCH-WINS, so the SPA catch-all must stay last or it
swallows the API. Everything dynamic proxies to the same Cloud Run service,
which means the browser sees ONE origin: no CORS preflight on any API call,
_comment_headers: Vite emits content-hashed asset filenames, so /assets/* can be immutable for
a year -- a changed file gets a new name. index.html must NOT be cached, or
the CDN keeps serving an old document pointing at deleted asset hashes, which
is the classic 'deployed but users see the old app' failure.
